verdict.rationale: Hoppscotch documents self-hosting on your own infrastructure with full data ownership. The Community Edition is MIT-licensed, the Enterprise Edition is a self-hosted version of Cloud, and there is a self-host admin dashboard. A community user independently confirms it "can be self-hosted", though they note desktop-app login does not work against self-hosted instances, and a GitHub issue reports a magic-link email failure on a self-hosted setup. missing for 10: concrete deployment documentation (install method, requirements) in the evidence, a working desktop-app login against self-hosted instances, and evidence the self-hosted auth/email flow works reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self-host Hoppscotch on your own infrastructure with full data ownership.
Hoppscotch Community Edition is free and open-source. It is licensed under the MIT License.
You can manage your server configurations directly from the self-host admin dashboard.
It has a clean UI and can be self-hosted.
